messages:
sam: Spawning RC from main -> 1.13.0-rc1. This includes the DB schema toggle for the sharded-metrics migration. Need fast QA signoff and ops confirmation we can flip the flag during canary. Target promo window 11:00 UTC. @ops-eli can you verify migration readiness?

claire: QA will run the migration-safe smoke and the query profile tests now. I'll post quick results.

ops-eli: Checking migration health: all nodes patched, background migration job has <1% backlog. Safe to flip flag in a 10% canary. I'll set db-shard-toggle=off by default and enable at canary.

deploy-bot: [build pinned] artifact=redwood-service:1.13.0-rc1 sha=sha256:aa1122 scheduled_promo=2026-04-10T11:00:00Z status=ready notes="includes db-shard-toggle support"

drv-qa: migration-smoke started. Running long-tail query sweep and ingest probe.

drv-qa: quick snapshot: ingest probe OK, tail queries within baseline, but noticed 0.3% 5xxs from a single read replica during heavy read test. tagging logs:
```
2026-04-10T10:05:12Z replica-7 read-error=504 trace=abcd1234
2026-04-10T10:05:13Z read-latency p95=420ms (baseline 200ms)
```

sam: Hmm. Could be replica transient. @ops-eli can you investigate replica-7? If it's noisy we'll route canary away and proceed. If not, we hold.

ops-eli: replica-7 shows elevated IO wait, rebalancing started. I'll remove replica-7 from replica set for canary traffic and re-route reads to repl-2 and repl-4. Will also warm DB cache.

claire: re-running migration-smoke after replica routing change.

drv-qa: re-smoke: all checks pass, no read errors, query p95 back to 190ms. migration toggle dry-run simulated OK. :white_check_mark:

sam: Product signoff from me: ready. Ops + QA thumbs up. Scheduling promo at 11:00 UTC. Please ensure the promo config includes a metric guard on db.read.errors and schema-mismatch detector.

deploy-bot: [promo scheduled] artifact=redwood-service:1.13.0-rc1 promo_time=2026-04-10T11:00:00Z steps=[canary(10%)->bump(25%)->full(100%)] rollback_command=`deployctl rollback --to=stable --from=1.13.0-rc1` checks=[metric_rule(db.read.errors>0.5% for 2m)->auto-stop, schema_delta_detector->alert]

migdb-bot: schema-delta-check: no breaking schema changes detected between stable and 1.13.0-rc1.

ops-eli: I'll be oncall for the window. Pager set to "release-sheriff". I'll flip `db-shard-toggle` to true at canary start and monitor replication lag.

sam: final: eng:+1, qa:+1, ops:+1. Proceed at 11.

deploy-bot: [promo started] step=canary target=10% started_at=2026-04-10T11:00:02Z

deploy-bot: [canary update] 10% 45s steady, errors=0.2% db.read.errors, schema-check OK, p95=210ms

ops-eli: replication lag spike observed on primary during deploy but within auto-heal thresholds. Keeping flag enabled for canary.

claire: I'm seeing a small spike in query time on one endpoint that uses the new sharded index, p95 ~320ms. Comparing traces now.

drv-qa: traces show a retry loop caused by an unexpected index ordering in that shard; it's not a full failure but increases latency.

sam: Given it's a latency-only, non-error issue for a small subset, propose we pause at 25% bump and ship a fast patch (ordering fix) as a rollforward rather than rolling back. Thoughts?

ops-eli: I prefer rollback for unknown DB risks, but this looks contained and non-corrupting. If we can push a hotfix within 15m and promote after verification, that's fine. Add stricter auto-stop: if db.read.errors > 1% or replication lag > 5s persist for 2m -> auto-rollback.

deploy-bot: [promo update] step=bump target=25% started_at=2026-04-10T11:06:30Z 25% steady 1m, db.read.errors=0.25%, p95=235ms

sam: OK Claire/Jamal, can you cut a tiny patch branch that flips index ordering in the shard handler and build a new rc1a? We'll pin if green.

claire: on it, creating patch branch and running unit + smoke.

deploy-bot: [build queued] artifact=redwood-service:1.13.0-rc1a base=1.13.0-rc1 sha=sha256:bb3344 status=building

claire: rc1a smoke local looks good, reran the slow endpoint tests. pushing artifact now.

deploy-bot: [build pinned] artifact=redwood-service:1.13.0-rc1a sha=sha256:bb3344 scheduled_promo=immediate replace=1.13.0-rc1

ops-eli: Can we swap the canary to rc1a at 25% without rolling back? Prefer hot-swap to avoid user impact.

sam: Yes, let's hot-swap canary. Deploy-bot, replace canary artifact and continue bump to 50% after 2m of steady telemetry.

deploy-bot: [hot-swap] replaced artifact at 25% canary -> redwood-service:1.13.0-rc1a switched_at=2026-04-10T11:12:10Z

deploy-bot: [canary update] rc1a 25% 90s steady, db.read.errors=0.1%, p95=200ms, schema OK

oncall-ops: monitoring looks good, no replication lag issues.

deploy-bot: [promo update] step=bump target=50% started_at=2026-04-10T11:15:00Z 50% steady 2m, errors=0.05%, p95=190ms

sam: great. Proceed to full.

deploy-bot: [promo update] step=full target=100% started_at=2026-04-10T11:20:30Z full steady, errors=0.02%, p95=188ms

ops-eli: post-deploy db checks passing. Rolling daily migration job back to nominal cadence.

sam: publishing release notes: "1.13.0-rc1 -> includes DB sharded-metrics toggle, index ordering fix (rc1a), minor perf tuning." Also noting the rollforward path used for canary hot-swap.

claire: QA ack and closing thread. If anything unusual appears, follow rollback_command or open incident.

deploy-bot: [promo complete] artifact=redwood-service:1.13.0-rc1a promoted_at=2026-04-10T11:21:05Z status=promoted

sam: thanks everyone. We'll monitor for 60m post-promote and then cut final release if stable. :rocket:
